channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Rams placed OL Justin Dedich on the non-football injury list.
item.description: Dedich played in 16 games for the Rams last year, including six starts. The then-second-year player earned a 69.7 PFF run-blocking grade along the way. The Rams also placed rookie DB Al’zillion Hamilton on the physically unable to perform list.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Broncos placed LB Jordan Turner on the non-football injury list.
item.description: The Denver Post’s Luca Evans describes the development as being “potentially quite notable” for the Broncos’ inside linebacker depth. He believes Turner “had a real shot” to win the No. 3 role behind LB Alex Singleton and LB Justin Strnad. Perhaps he still can. Only time will tell. The Broncos also placed OG Nick Gargiulo on the physically unable to perform list.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Jaguars placed LT Cole Van Lanen on the physically unable to perform list with a knee injury.
item.description: Van Lanen took snaps at four-of-five offensive line spots last season before ultimately settling in as a breakout left tackle. The Jaguars rewarded him with a three-year, $51 million extension on January 2nd. The knee injury he is currently recovering from occurred on January4th. According to Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley, Van Lanen “did not do much during the offseason program, and it remains to be seen exactly what his timeline looks like.” Whether he starts in Week 1 against the Browns is unknown.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Lions placed S Kerby Joseph on the physically unable to perform list with a knee injury.
item.description: Just yesterday, Joseph implied via social media that he would avoid the physically unable to perform list. So much for that. Joseph dealt with a recurring knee issue for the entire 2025 season, which was first reported on at the end of July 2025, roughly three months after the Lions made him the NFL’s highest-paid safety. Given Joseph’s post, one imagines he has a chance to resume practicing relatively soon, but only time will tell. Branch suffered an Achilles tendon rupture in Week 14 last year. As of June 13th, Lions coach Dan Campbell said there was no timetable for his return. The Lions also placed TE Tyler Conklin on the physically unable to perform list.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: ESPN’s Mike Reiss reports that Patriots WR Kayshon Boutte “delivered highlight plays each of the first two days of training camp.”
item.description: Boutte has been getting behind the Patriots’ defense thus far, maintaining the positive downfield play he demonstrated last season. The fourth-year wide receiver was the subject of trade rumors earlier this offseason. Training camp hype could get that news cycle going again. That said, having a deep receiving corps is a great problem to have. If Boutte is willing to buy into a rotational WR3/4 role behind WR1 A.J. Brown and WR2 Romeo Doubs, keeping Boutte in a Patriots uniform could be best for all involved. It will be very difficult for him to warrant FLEX treatment in re-draft formats with his current squad, though.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: The Athletic’s Matt Barrows reports that 49ers WR Christian Kirk “walked off with a trainer midway through the session” on Sunday.
item.description: Kirk, 29, is entering his ninth NFL season. As is often the case with NFL veterans, Kirk has picked up his fair share of injuries over the years, including two hamstring strains last season. Fortunately, we are a long way from Week 1. There is no cause for concern at this time. 49ers acting head coach Chris Foerster will address the media shortly, so we could have clarity as to what the issue is soon.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that the Cardinals and QB Jacoby Brissett “reached agreement today on a reworked contract.”
item.description: Brissett was scheduled to make up to $4.88 this year, in the final year of his old deal. His new contract increases his compensation for this season, but he is still scheduled to hit free agency next offseason. The new deal includes a $15.5 million base salary. He can make up to $21 million via incentives. Things can always change in-season, but this appears to be clear-cut starter money — and it’s good news for Cardinals pass catchers. Although the Cardinals struggled to win games with Brissett under center last year, he was a very productive passer. Theoretically, he should be able to support TE Trey McBride and likely one of WR Marvin Harrison Jr. or WR Michael Wilson reliably. Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur confirmed that the plan is for Brissett to start in Week 1 against the Chargers.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: 49ers re-signed DL Kevin Givens.
item.description: A 2019 undrafted free agent, Givens, 29, has spent his entire career with the 49ers. He logged defensive snaps in 13 games over the past two seasons, partially due to a pair of pectoral injuries. He will now compete for a role as a rotational interior pass rusher. Hopefully, the pectoral issues are behind him.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: The Athletic’s Matt Barrows reports Nick Bosa (knee) has been cleared for practice.
item.description: Barrows notes that Bosa will “likely get ramped up in practice over the next two weeks or so.” It doesn’t sound like he’s expected to be a full go just yet, but it’s always a good sign for a player coming off an ACL tear in the previous season when he avoids the PUP list to start camp. Bosa totaled two sacks and nine tackles in just three games last season, but had totaled nine or more sacks in each of his previous four seasons. Still only 28 years old, Bosa should have plenty to offer the Niners’ defense once he’s back in full and getting after the quarterback.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports “Washington is intriguing” to free agent WR Stefon Diggs.
item.description: The opportunity to play with Jayden Daniels and spend a season playing in front of his hometown could be enough to entice Diggs, a DMV native, to join the Commanders. There are reportedly four other teams that have also expressed interest in the 32-year-old receiver, but a signing does not appear imminent at this time. Diggs is nearly two years removed from the torn ACL that ended his 2024 season, and he still managed to post an 85-1,013-4 line in his lone season with the Patriots while appearing on just 55 percent of the team’s offensive snaps. We would expect the veteran receiver to find a new home sooner than later, especially with all teams set to being training camp later this week.-Zachary Krueger
